Claire — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marcus (infra lead) and Grace (privacy/product) so we can provide the annotated flow and KMS specifics.

Quick answers up front while we assemble artifacts:
- Persistence: Redwood keeps raw user input in ephemeral request-level memory (max 120s) and KV caches for active sessions. Long-term stores (for audit/analytics) are opt-in and require explicit customer consent in the console; default is no long-term storage.
- Redaction/tokenization: By default we hash and token-map high-risk PII at the ingress layer for hosted customers when toggled in the policy (customer-configurable). KV cache entries are encrypted at rest and are not exported by default.
- KMS: For Redwood Private we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS) and Redwood-managed KMS for hosted. Marcus will provide the KMS export/rotation details and a short diagram showing which services hold decrypt privileges.

We will attach an annotated single-page dataflow (redwood-dataflow-annotated-v1.pdf) and a completed SSQ answers spreadsheet. Expect the delivery by end of day Monday.

Priya
Priya Natarajan

Claire — adding the infra specifics you requested. High level:

- Ephemeral runtime: model servers (inference pods) hold request plaintext only in memory; we configure a strict TTL of 120s for in-memory artifacts and eviction on completion. No disk persistence in the runtime path.
- KV cache: used to accelerate multi-turn chats. Keys stored in the KV cache are encrypted with tenant keys; we maintain per-tenant encryption keys derived from the KMS root. Cache TTL is customer-configurable (default 2 hours).
- Long-term stores: Audit logs and aggregated telemetry (token counts, latencies) are retained in separate analytics buckets (not linked to PII unless customer opts in). We provide field-level pseudonymization for any audit exports.
- KMS & key custody: For Private deployments we provide an HSM/KMS integration guide. Customer-managed keys are supported (you control root key and rotation). For Hosted customers, keys are Redwood-managed but we provide key rotation attestations and exportable audit logs.

Attached: redwood-dataflow-annotated-v1.pdf (single-page dataflow with redaction gates highlighted) and redwood-ssq-answers-20270516.xlsx (SSQ answers with references to DPA sections).

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — that helps a lot. A couple follow-ups after reviewing the attachments:

1) The annotated flow shows KV cache TTL as "customer-configurable (default 2h)" — for ClearMed we need a maximum allowed TTL of 30 minutes for any KV that includes PHI. Is that a configuration you can gate at the tenant policy level?

2) For hosted customers, can you share the specific artifact/location of the key rotation attestations (we need an export for our vendor inventory)?

3) On the redaction side: we noticed the ingress hash process still preserves a last-4 pattern for some identifiers in the cache for session continuity. We need a mapping of which built-in redaction rules preserve any partial patterns (last-4, domain-preserve, etc.) so we can confirm compliance.

If you can confirm (1) we can proceed with the DPA appendix acceptance pending the DocuSign. For (2) and (3) we just need links or short proof artifacts — a rotation ledger export and a redaction-rule matrix.

Thanks,
Claire
